Theme

Household, washing & chores · Nature & food

fire noun

flames; something burning

also a fire, the fire, on fire, catch fire, blaze, campfire, put out a fire, extinguish a fire

classical

Ter. Eun. 85: accēde ad ignem hunc
Cic. Off. 1.52: patī ab igne ignem capere

ignis, ignis m.

noun, third declension

Fire in general, and the fire one sits by or cooks on; to light one is ignem excitāre (see kindle a fire).

Other words

  • incendium, incendiī n. — a fire that destroys, a blaze

    noun, second declension · classical · Traupman 167, 315: fire, incendium; put out a fire, incendium exstinguere; Publ. S 48: vīcīnum velle ulcīscī incendiō

    A house or a forest on fire.

  • ārdeō, ārdēre, ārsī, ārsum — be on fire, burn

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 315: be on fire, ārdeō; Hor. S. 1.5.72: paene macrōs ārsit

Examples

  • Bonō animō es: accēde ad ignem hunc; jam calēscēs plūs satis

    cheer up: come to this fire; you’ll soon be more than warm enoughTer. Eun. 84–85

  • stultum est vīcīnum velle ulcīscī incendiō

    it is foolish to take revenge on a neighbour by firePubl. S 48

  • sēdulus hospes paene macrōs ārsit dum turdōs versat in ignī

    our busy host nearly went up in flames while turning some skinny thrushes on the fireHor. S. 1.5.71–72

  • incendium exstinguere

    to put out a fireTraupman 167

See also kindle a fire, flame, hearth, fireplace, smoke, fire engine, fire station, firefighter, burn, burn.
